contributions.statement: For ingesting lecture video, audio or scanned material, have a sandboxed text+image coding agent write extraction code (ffmpeg keyframes, ASR transcripts, OCR, timestamps) and reason over those artifacts rather than feeding raw media to a native multimodal model; Codex with GPT-5.4 reached 75.0% vs 66.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro on OmniGAIA while using far fewer input tokens.
contributions.evidence: §2.1 Table 1 and Fig. 3 (token usage); text-only ablation shows many items are solvable via OCR/transcripts, and vision-centric benchmarks drop sharply. Single pass@1 runs with web access.

contributions.statement: Skills distilled from the agent's own execution traces beat human-written and binary-feedback self-iterated skills.
contributions.evidence: §2.3 Fig. 7, App. H.2: 61.4% to 76.7% on OmniGAIA in the best setting; one model, single run, skills likely mined on the evaluation benchmark.

reason: Out of the SE domain, but it gives a direct design choice for multimedia cross-repository work: extract with code, then reason over text. The skill-distillation result lacks a held-out split.
